findings.claim: The customManager regex `(?<currentValue>v?[0-9][^\\s]*)` requires the `# tag:` comment value to begin with `v` or a digit. The SCP self-dogfood wrapper's actual comment is `# tag: post-v1.0.0 + warn-msg fix (020D1.1)`, which begins with `p`. The regex will not match; Renovate will not auto-bump SHA or comment-tag on SCP's own wrapper. Sub-criterion (ii) (bumps SHA + comment-tag together) is non-functional on the only concrete test fixture. Sub-criterion (vi) (in-WP cascade validation) demonstrates structural composition (extends present) but not the automation path.
findings.evidence: renovate/default.json customManagers[0].matchStrings: `...#\\s*tag:\\s*(?<currentValue>v?[0-9][^\\s]*)` — pattern anchored at `v?[0-9]`. policy-check-wrapper.yml line 47: `# tag: post-v1.0.0 + warn-msg fix (020D1.1)` — starts with literal `p`. Pattern requires first non-optional character to be a digit or `v`; `p` does not satisfy either branch.
findings.impact: Renovate will silently skip the SCP self-consumer wrapper on every scheduled run. SHA pins will not be auto-bumped. The DISPATCH-NOTE checklist items (ii) and (vi) are checked ✅ on the basis of the regex having both capture groups — but the groups are unreachable on the real file. Adopters who correctly format their `# tag: <semver>` comment will be fine; SCP's own wrapper is the broken case, which undermines the stated in-WP validation goal.
findings.mitigation: Fix the wrapper `# tag:` comment to a proper semver value (e.g. `v1.0.0`) matching the canonical adopter pattern shown in 020H part 3. Alternatively, widen the currentValue regex to `(?<currentValue>[^\\s]+)` and add a separate versioningTemplate that tolerates arbitrary strings — but the simpler fix is to align the wrapper comment to the documented convention. Fix must be verified by a test invocation or Renovate dry-run showing both capture groups populated.

Prior slices (020J, 020H part 1, 020H part 2) treat tag-cutting as part of the slice, not a deferred step. Diverging from that pattern without an explicit tracked-forward item or post-merge hook creates an accountability gap.
findings.mitigation: Do not descope. Change the checklist item to `- [ ] (iii) POST-MERGE: cut renovate/v1.0.0 tag (see Tag series section)` to accurately represent the state. Add a named tracked-forward item TF-020F-001 in the DISPATCH-NOTE or STATUS.md with owner=jrnb2024 and a concrete post-merge action line. Alternatively, cut the tag on a branch commit before merge so the checklist tick is truthful.

findings.claim: Plan §4 020F sub-criterion (i) states: `github>jrnb2024/standards-control-plane//renovate/default#<tag>` — missing the trailing `-` in the repo name (correct name: `standards-control-plane-`). The same error appears in plan §4 020H part 3's canonical adopter wrapper snippet: `depName=jrnb2024/standards-control-plane` (no trailing dash). Adopters who copy from plan text rather than from the shipped ADOPT-001 appendix will build non-matching annotation comments; their SHA pins will not be picked up by the customManager.
findings.evidence: Plan §4 020F (i): `github>jrnb2024/standards-control-plane//renovate/default#<tag>`. Plan §4 020H part 3 wrapper snippet: `# renovate: datasource=github-tags depName=jrnb2024/standards-control-plane`. renovate/default.json depNameTemplate: `jrnb2024/standards-control-plane` (trailing dash present). renovate.json extends: `github>jrnb2024/standards-control-plane//renovate/default` (trailing dash present). Implementation is correct; plan text is wrong.
findings.impact: Low immediate impact (020H part 3 is unshipped; no adopters are currently using the plan spec text as their sole reference). Elevated impact when 020H part 3 ships if it inherits the plan's typo — the canonical adopter wrapper snippet will contain a broken annotation that no Renovate regex will ever match.
findings.mitigation: Correct plan §4 020F (i) and 020H part 3 wrapper snippet to use `standards-control-plane-` consistently. Grep the full plan document for `standards-control-plane` (without trailing dash) to find all occurrences. Since the plan is already merged, the correction should go into a docs-only PR or be absorbed into the 020H part 3 authoring process.

findings.claim: The `renovate/v*` tag series has no GitHub tag-protection ruleset. The 020J ruleset protects `refs/tags/v*` but the pattern `v*` is a literal-prefix match (no slash), so `renovate/v1.0.0` is outside its scope. The DISPATCH-NOTE acknowledges this as intentional deferral (`If we wanted preset tag protection, we'd add a second ruleset ... in a follow-up slice. Not in 020F scope.`) but names no specific follow-up slice and creates no tracked-forward item.
findings.evidence: DISPATCH-NOTE.md Tag series section: `The renovate/v* tag series is intentionally outside this protection — it represents preset shape ... If we wanted preset tag protection, we'd add a second ruleset matching refs/tags/renovate/v* in a follow-up slice.` No TF-NNN or follow-up slice is named. STATUS.md Open scheduled follow-ups table does not include renovate/v* tag protection.
findings.impact: Any maintainer (today: jrnb2024 only; post-estate-rollout: potentially others with repo admin) can delete or force-push `renovate/v1.0.0` without any governance barrier. For adopters pinning `#renovate/v1.0.0` in their `extends:`, a tag repoint is a silent supply-chain substitution. The deferral is acceptable for a single-operator personal account but the absence of a named follow-up means the gap has no closure path.
findings.mitigation: Add a named tracked-forward item (e.g. TF-020F-002: add refs/tags/renovate/v* protection ruleset) to STATUS.md Open scheduled follow-ups, with a target window (suggest: before first estate consumer extends the preset at a pinned tag). This preserves the deferral without losing the accountability thread.

findings.claim: DISPATCH-NOTE sub-criterion (vii) closes U-sec-3 and U-gov-1 by assertion: `Renovate Bot already active on jrnb2024 per WP-SCP-020 §6 (Mend hosted app).` No verification artifact is present in the slice (no API response, no Renovate dashboard screenshot, no installation-ID reference, no Renovate PR generated against SCP). Prior slices that closed governance items (020E.b, 020E.c) committed canary-evidence.md with run-IDs. U-sec-3 + U-gov-1 receive only a verbal assertion.
findings.evidence: DISPATCH-NOTE.md item (vii): single-sentence assertion with back-reference to plan §6. No artifact in docs/reviews/WP-SCP-022/dispatches/020f/ corroborating Renovate app installation or a successful Renovate dry-run against the SCP repo.
findings.impact: If the Renovate app is not active on jrnb2024 at the time adopters extend the preset, no PRs will be generated — the cascade automation silently does not exist. Without an evidence artifact, post-merge verification of the U-sec-3 + U-gov-1 closure is not independently reproducible.
findings.mitigation: Add a minimal evidence entry to DISPATCH-NOTE.md or a companion artifact file: e.g. paste the Renovate dashboard URL for jrnb2024/standards-control-plane, the installation ID from GitHub Settings → Applications → Renovate, or (preferably) trigger a Renovate dry-run (`renovate --dry-run`) and commit the log showing the repo is discovered and the config parses without error. This is low-effort and closes the assertion gap.

findings.claim: DISPATCH-NOTE.md slice acceptance checklist has no item committing to a post-merge STATUS.md update. STATUS.md currently shows 020F as a post-Threshold-A backlog item (`020F: Renovate shared preset`). The established pattern across all prior slices (020J, 020K, 020D1, 020H part 1, 020D2, etc.) is that STATUS.md is updated in the merge commit or same-session follow-up. The omission creates a risk that STATUS.md remains stale post-merge.
findings.evidence: DISPATCH-NOTE.md checklist: seven items (i)–(vii), no STATUS.md update item. STATUS.md line 102: `020F: Renovate shared preset.` listed under post-Threshold-A backlog with no in-flight marker. Prior pattern: STATUS.md updated within same session as each slice.
findings.impact: Low — STATUS.md is a human-readable dashboard, not a machine-consumed artefact. However, for a programme this governance-dense, a stale STATUS.md creates confusion about which slices are live and which are pending for anyone reading the repo post-020F.
findings.mitigation: Add a checklist item to DISPATCH-NOTE.md: `- [ ] Post-merge: update STATUS.md to mark 020F landed and advance post-Threshold-A backlog row.` Trivial to add before merge.

findings.claim: The `renovate.json` `extends:` entry (`github>jrnb2024/standards-control-plane//renovate/default`) carries no `#<tag>` pin and is not covered by the customManager (which only matches workflow `uses:` patterns via managerFilePatterns). When `renovate/v2.0.0` ships, Renovate will not open a PR to bump SCP-self's `extends:` reference — nor will it do so for adopters who pin their `extends:` with `#renovate/v1.0.0`. The DISPATCH-NOTE does not discuss this asymmetry.
findings.criterion: sub-criterion (vi) — automation asymmetry on extends: field
findings.evidence: renovate/default.json managerFilePatterns: `/\.github/workflows/.*\.ya?ml$/` — scoped to workflow YAML only. renovate.json: `"extends": ["github>jrnb2024/standards-control-plane//renovate/default"]` — no `#<tag>` suffix. No packageRule or customManager entry targets `renovate.json` or the `extends:` field. Renovate does not have a built-in manager for the `extends:` field in `renovate.json` files.
findings.impact: Very low for SCP-self (tracking HEAD is the self-consumer pattern). Non-trivial for adopters: if an adopter pins `extends: ["github>jrnb2024/standards-control-plane//renovate/default#renovate/v1.0.0"]`, they have no automation path to bump to `#renovate/v2.0.0`. The customManager only bumps workflow SHA pins. This design gap means preset version upgrades are a manual step for adopters, contradicting the estate-cascade automation promise.
findings.mitigation: Document the limitation explicitly in DISPATCH-NOTE.md and/or the upcoming 020H part 3 adopter appendix: preset version bumps in `extends:` are manual; SHA pin bumps in wrapper `uses:` are automated. If automated extends-version bumping is desired, a separate customManager targeting `renovate.json` files in downstream repos (matching `github>jrnb2024/standards-control-plane//renovate/default#(?<currentValue>renovate/v[^"]+)`) would be needed — but that manager would need to live in adopter repos, not in the SCP preset itself.

structured_review.summary: Three MAJ findings block acceptance. The most critical (COMP-001) is a functional defect: the customManager regex in renovate/default.json cannot match the SCP self-dogfood wrapper's non-semver `# tag:` comment, meaning the in-WP cascade validation (sub-criterion vi) demonstrates the preset structure but not the automation path. The checklist pre-ticks sub-criterion (iii) before the renovate/v1.0.0 tag exists. The adopter marker convention is undocumented (020H part 3 not yet shipped), so the customManager has no documented adoption path. Two MIN findings (spec-text repo-name error; unprotected renovate/v* series with no named follow-up) and two nits complete the picture.
